simple.meaning: קָטַר (qâṭar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to inclose.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 46:22. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָטַר (H7000) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: קָטַר (qâṭar) / H7000 is traced through Ezekiel 46:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: In the four corners of the court there were courts enclosed, forty cubits* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. long and thirty wide. These four in the corners were the same size.
